Subject: Brightlane pilot — discovery recap & next steps

Hi Alyssa,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate you walking us through Brightlane's latency SLAs and the projected burst patterns for the recommendation API. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Goal: Proof-of-concept to validate 95th percentile latency < 120ms at peak and 3x daily batch jobs for nightly scoring.
- Scope: 2 model variants (high-accuracy and quantized low-cost) + KV cache for session reuse.
- Metric success: P95 latency, tokens/sec cost, and integration effort for your ops team.

Attachments: I pushed a brief usage estimate and a preliminary pricing quote — redwood-usage-estimate-Brightlane.xlsx and redwood-pricing-quote-BL-v1.pdf.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick internal alignment on SOW and who signs — is procurement the right owner or do you want engineering to greenlight the integration?
2) Pilot kick-off week: Oct 6 (we can shift if you need earlier EoQ handling).
3) 30–45 minute runbook/hand-off with your infra lead once the reserved capacity is provisioned.

If approvals/budget are tight at the end of the quarter, we can scope a smaller pilot (single model, 2-week run) to get the latency numbers quickly — happy to discuss trade-offs.

Thoughts? Happy to jump on a 15-min call to finalize timeline.

Cheers,

Short answers below and attached a 1-page note for procurement: redwood-pricing-quote-BL-v1.pdf (high/low cost scenarios based on the traffic buckets you shared) and redwood-usage-estimate-Brightlane.xlsx (token/time breakdowns).

1) Cost ranges (6-week pilot):
   - Best-case: ~$6.8k (quantized + aggressive prefix caching, lower burst)
   - Mid-case: ~$11.5k (mix of variants, typical burst)
   - Worst-case: ~$19.2k (higher traffic + high-accuracy model use)

2) KV cache: Integration is lightweight — you only need to pass session keys and a small prefix (no schema changes to your DB). We can run a 30-min tech sync with Mark to demo.

3) Approval path: If procurement owns legal/PO, Procurement is the right routing. If you need a PO before provisioning, we can do a limited-commit pilot with a cap and auto-stop.
